role.altitude: The supervisor's week is still the floor, the pass and the menu meeting. Less of it is rebuilding last week's sellers from memory, or chasing a due date that was never written down. The meeting, the walk and the repair call stay with the supervisor.
reach: Cooks and food preparation workers: the agreed menu and the fault note, before service starts
Serving staff: the serving arrangements and allergen wording for tonight's dishes
skills_to_grow: Hear a machine fault on the walk before the due date says it is time
Keep a price change and an allergen change inside the menu meeting, on the same sheet
Refuse a repair call that does not name the machine and the fault just seen
role.ambitious_version: Before the menu meeting the sheet already shows what sold, what was wasted, and a portion cost. The maintenance list shows which machines are due. The supervisor still runs the meeting, still walks the line, and still calls the engineer.

tasks.short: Menu meetings with kitchen and floor on dishes and service

steps.what: Pull sellers and waste from the point-of-sale before menu planning.
Draft menu options and serving arrangements on a sheet.
Conduct meetings and collaborate with kitchen and floor personnel.
Write the related details agreed in the meeting onto the sheet.
Send the serving plan to the other station personnel.

tasks.design: Before the meeting, a {SPREADSHEET} fed from the point-of-sale ({OTHER}) lists what sold and what was wasted, and a portion cost from ingredient prices sits beside the current dishes on a {DOCS} sheet. The meeting stays a meeting. Afterwards the agreed dishes, the serving arrangements and the allergen wording are one sheet, sent to the kitchen and the floor. Use the sheet the site already has before any custom code. The note records the decision, not who spoke.
tasks.previous_blocker: The menu lived in people's heads and on a paper card, so each meeting started by reconstructing what sold.
tasks.enabler_now: Till totals and a stored recipe cost can sit on one sheet before anyone sits down.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what the kitchen can hold, and what the floor can explain, only happens with those people in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor hears which dish the cook will not stand behind and which special the floor cannot describe.

ambition.what: Replan one dish the same day a seller dies, because last week's numbers are already on the sheet.

tasks.altitude: The meeting stays the work. The sheet before it is shorter, and the write-up after it is one page.

reach.task: Agree the dishes and the prices in the menu meeting
reach.learn: Which dishes the kitchen can actually hold on a busy service

reach.task: Carry the serving arrangements onto the floor
reach.learn: Which specials and allergens guests will ask about tonight

evidence.claim: Ingredient prices can roll up to a portion cost on the sheet the meeting reads. That figure does not choose the dish, and it is not a measure of meeting time.

Guests must receive information on the 14 EU allergens. In 2022 only 41% of inspected horeca complied, and the information was often not available in writing or electronically, so a person checks the wording of a changed dish before it is sent.
Works-council consent covers systems that monitor staff behaviour or performance, so the meeting note records the decision and not a score of who spoke.
No source in this digest measures how long a menu meeting takes, so the time split is a judgement of the steps.

assumptions: The prior puts about 77% of this task on meetings in person and calls the main shape workflow automation. The meeting itself is left at 62% and is not automated. The sheet before it and the note after it are the rest.
Colleagues' hours in the room are not part of this role's baseline, so they are not saved here.
Portion cost on the sheet is a figure for the discussion. It is not counted as time saved.
The prior's mail share is about 7%. The send step is 8%. The meeting is not treated as mail.
A head chef's extra signature is not in today's steps, so none is added. Steady upkeep is two hours per 100 baseline hours to correct a dish name or an allergen line after the meeting.
unknowns: Whether a head chef must sign a menu change before it reaches the floor.
Which written form this site uses for allergen information at the pass.
research_questions: How often does this site change the menu, and who else must agree before a dish is served?

already_counted.description: The supervisor still glances at the seller list before the meeting.
The supervisor still edits the draft sheet so it matches what the kitchen can cook.
The menu meeting itself still happens with kitchen and floor personnel.
The supervisor still writes the agreed dishes and the allergen lines onto the sheet.
The supervisor still checks the sent plan before the stations see it.

incremental.description: After the meeting the supervisor corrects a wrong dish name or an allergen line on the sheet.
A cook recopies one special onto the pass board when the sheet changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week with one menu meeting and a stable card saves the pre-read and the send. A week that replans several dishes keeps almost all of the meeting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintenance schedules for kitchen equipment and the repair call

steps.what: Read equipment fault notes left since the last visit.
Develop equipment maintenance schedules for the coming month.
Walk the line and judge which equipment needs repairs.
Arrange repairs with the service firm for that machine.
File the visit on the equipment maintenance log.

tasks.design: A {SPREADSHEET} holds each machine and its interval and rolls the next due date forward. Fault notes stay a written list until the supervisor has read them. The supervisor still walks the line, still decides a machine cannot wait, and still calls the service firm. That call is allowed only for the machine and the fault confirmed on the walk; any change to the fault means the call is not covered. The visit is then written on a {DOCS} log that names the machine and the fault, not a member of staff. Configure that log before writing a new app.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due dates sat on a paper list, and a repair was arranged only after a machine had already failed on service.
tasks.enabler_now: Intervals can roll forward on a sheet, so the month's due machines are visible before the walk.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing a fault, and deciding a machine cannot wait, still takes a person on the line.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor knows which noise is a worn seal and which noise is a machine that will stop mid-service.

ambition.what: Call the service firm in the week a machine is due, instead of after it fails on a busy service.

tasks.altitude: The walk and the call stay. The due list and the log take less rewriting.

reach.task: Leave a fault note when a machine misbehaves
reach.learn: Which noises and temperature drifts mean a real fault

reach.task: Carry out the repair on the agreed visit
reach.learn: Which parts fail together on this site's machines

evidence.claim: No source in this digest measures supervisor time on maintenance schedules or repair calls, so the time split is a judgement of the steps.
Works-council consent covers systems fit to monitor attendance, behaviour or performance, so the equipment log names the machine and the fault and does not rank a worker.

Annex III covers allocating tasks by individual behaviour or traits and monitoring performance, and that employment use applies from 2 December 2027. A calendar of machine service does neither, and this design does not rank staff for shifts.
A decision based solely on automated processing is barred where it has a significant effect, so the repair call is placed by the supervisor after the walk and is not sent by a rule alone.

assumptions: The prior puts about 62% on meetings in person. That time is the floor walk at 42% and the repair call at 20%, not a sit-down meeting.
The schedule step is 16%, above the prior's spreadsheet share of about 9%, because writing the month's dates is the part that can shrink. Fault notes and the log carry the document share.

The prior's external reach matches the repair call. The supervisor confirms the fault on the walk, which already happens, and that confirmation is the approval. A manager's second signature is not in today's steps.
A capital replacement, as against a service visit, is outside this task and would need a higher approval this graph does not include.

Upkeep of three hours per 100 baseline hours is the steady correction of due dates and one chased visit, not the build. No model loop is used: the dates are interval arithmetic and the fault is judged on the walk.
unknowns: Whether a maintenance contract already sets the visit days.
What spend a supervisor may commit on a repair without a manager.
research_questions: Which machines are on a contract, and which repairs the supervisor may order alone?

already_counted.description: The supervisor still reads the fault notes before building the month.
The supervisor still moves a due date when the kitchen cannot spare the machine.
The floor walk still happens, and that walk is the confirmation behind the repair call.
The supervisor still spends the call explaining the fault and agreeing the visit.
The supervisor still checks the log line after the visit is agreed.

incremental.description: Each month the supervisor corrects a due date and chases one missed visit.
The service firm confirms the visit window after the call.

approvals.approved_version: Repair request for the named machine, with the fault seen on the walk and the visit window, as the supervisor confirmed before calling.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A quiet month of scheduled services saves the date chase and the retyping of the log. A month with a breakdown keeps the walk and most of the call.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
